source: Yahoo Finance; FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

items.name: Brent–WTI spread
items.note: A wider spread makes US crude more attractive to export

items.name: Brent curve
items.note: Backwardation (near months dearer) signals a tight market; contango signals surplus

items.name: 3-2-1 crack spread
items.desc: US refining margin: RBOB gasoline and heating oil vs WTI, front month
items.note: A proxy for how profitable it is to refine a barrel of crude

items.name: JKM–TTF spread
items.desc: Asian LNG (JKM) minus European gas (TTF), front month
items.note: When Asia pays more than Europe, flexible LNG cargoes head east

items.name: Dry bulk freight
items.desc: Breakwave Dry Bulk Shipping ETF (proxy for Capesize, Panamax and Supramax rates)
items.note: An ETF proxy, as the Baltic indices are not freely available

items.name: Tanker freight
items.desc: Breakwave Tanker Shipping ETF (proxy for crude and product tanker rates)
items.note: An ETF proxy, as the Baltic indices are not freely available

not_covered: Baltic Dry and tanker indices (licensed; ETF proxies shown instead)

eia_weekly.avg_note: 5-year average for the same week of the year, previous five years

risk.name: Credit stress
risk.desc: US high-yield bond spread over Treasuries
risk.rule: Green below 4%, amber 4–6%, red above 6%. Also amber if the spread widens by more than 1 point in a month

risk.name: Recession signal
risk.rule: Green above 0.25 pts, amber 0–0.25, red when the curve inverts (below 0)

risk.name: Financial stress
risk.desc: St. Louis Fed Financial Stress Index (0 = average)
risk.rule: Green below 0 (calmer than average), amber 0–1, red above 1

risk.name: Dollar squeeze
risk.desc: Broad US dollar index, change over the past month
risk.rule: Green below +1.5% in a month, amber +1.5% to +3%, red above +3%
